The cycle lane ends abruptly and forces cyclists out into a single lane, high-traffic roadway or up onto the sidewalk.  This causes conflict with vehicles and pedestrians from there all the way down to Columbus Avenue. At about 5:15pm, while the sun was setting, a car heading east on Beacon St (coming downhill) did not stop at the red light at the Beacon/Charles intersection. It seemed the driver may have been "blinded" by the setting sun and it was terrifying to watch.
Especially as people gain speed going downhill on Beacon, there should be some sort of extra flashing light or speedbump or something to make it easier to see the red light at this time of day or slow down while traveling on Beacon St.
Thank you

There are several issues at this intersection; the MAIN one being that there is no safe part of the traffic light cycle for pedestrians to cross Warren street at this intersection. There are also no walk signals to cross Warren street or Kelton street, and the signal to cross Comm Ave is far too short, and often the T runs the light, meaning most of the time given to cross is wasted because it is blocked. 

This intersection is also dangerous to cars, since it is a merging/crossing of multiple lanes of traffic, all needing to yield to the Comm Ave service road cars, which does not always happen. Right of way is far from clear at this intersection when 6 lanes of traffic receive a green light at once, and each of them can choose one of 4 directions to go in.

This intersection has multiple streets meeting at the bottom of a hill.  Turns are sharp and cars drive way too fast for the road.   Streets are used at cut through by GPS apps. Area is 100% residential and drivers pay no regard for people walking or getting in and out of their cars. Dangerous

Every day I see multiple cars FLYING through red (not yellow) lights in ALL areas of Boston, and I've never once seen anyone pulled over. This combined with in-car "legal" pot smoking is a deadly combination. Why won't our police force do their job? It is illegal to smoke pot and drive. The police at Mass & Cass area already allow drug dealers to deal and junkies to shoot up in plain sight, so they're not busy with that. I see them sitting in their cars, looking at their phones most of the time.

properties.request_other: People constantly block this bike lane
properties.comments: This unprotected stretch of the bike lane is constantly full of idling cars.
Cars constantly park in these bike lanes. They need physical separation.

There are OK (unprotected) bike lanes coming from BU/Comm Ave, but once one enters the Kenmore intersection, it's the wild west. If there are bike lanes along Comm Ave here, they are not only completely unprotected, but are *always* occupied by cars, both single- and double-parked. That said, I don't believe there even are bike lanes here; I've certainly never seen them. So cyclists have to ride in the street with not only lots of compact traffic, but also people moving into/out of parking spaces and getting into/out of their cars. It's truly a horrendous stretch for cyclists. And forget it when there's a Red Sox game... Traffic becomes horrendous making things even more hazardous for cyclists.

And while it's currently under construction (so I kind of understand), the other side is just as bad: no real bike lanes with lots of traffic. It screams dangerous.

Every single time I pass by here (1-2x per week), the entire stretch of road is double parked. From the intersection at Comm Ave & Brookline St all the way to Charlesgate West. This is a nightmare for cyclists, not only forcing us further into the road, but causing concern with the likelihood for opening car doors.

There's even a BlueBikes stand at this corner, but the infrastructure is laughable. 

And I've just taken a look at the map, and there are actually bike lanes along this stretch. That's genuinely news to me. I don't think I've ever used/noticed them thanks to the abundance of double-parkers here.

Between Charlesgate West and Charlesgate East, there is a poorly painted bike lane (not great but at least it's something). But once cyclists cross Charlesgate East along Comm Ave, things become very tricky. 

The bike lane abruptly ends, turning into a "sharrow". This is awful. The streets are tight with aggressive drivers to the left and tons of parked cars that could open their doors at any moment on the right. This a large road with lots of traffic, including pedestrians, cyclists, and cars. There's no reason to have parking along Comm Ave at this part.

Perhaps even more confusing is that once you cross Charlesgate East, a painted bike lane suddenly appears along the left side of the road. I cannot for the life of me understand how someone this was a good idea. Cyclists would need to cross two lanes of traffic to get to this bike lane. Sure, one could get into position at the red light, but that's not only unreasonable to expect, but a cyclist may not get a red light to do so,
This bike lane is unprotected and perpetually encroached by cars.

There Is an island here with a Blue bikes station, however it lacks any curb cuts or crossings to it. How are people supposed to safely access this station? There also used to be a bus stop here and it seems like adding curb cuts and crossings would have been a better solution to the accessibility issues than removing it as the city has done. 

This is also the most direct route for pedestrians heading East on the south side of Boylston but the current infrastructure requires a detour or a potentially dangerous and inaccessible crossing.

This is probably the most encroach bike lane in the whole city. It needs physical separation, including hard vertical elements, to prevent cars from parking in the bike lane. If cars are physically able to do so they will block the bike lane on this stretch so it is crucial to make sure they are physically incapable of doing so.

I regularly pass through this intersection on a bike, as a pedestrian, and in a car. This is a genuinely dangerous intersection as Cars heading west on New Minton genuinely cannot see bikes/pedestrians headed south on the path until they are basically in the street. This should be a raised crossing for the path and have a stop sign for cars. I do not want to hit someone or be hit by someone here.

The curb cut and crosswalk here do not align with break in the half wall and connection to the path. People already regularly cross on the south side of Cornwall because it more directly aligns with that path. The existing configuration requires those walking on the south side of Cornwall, or trying to get there from the path to do 3 sides of a square to legally cross rather than taking that more direct route. This is even more of a problem for people on bikes because the turns are very tight, so most people just try to hop the curb instead (creating risks of falling into traffic).

There should be a curb cut and crossing aligned with the break in the half wall here. There should also be a stop sign at these crossings because cars frequently speed through this intersection to beat the lights on either side. The daylighting on the southern side of Cornwall should also be extended one space further back because the sight lines are still inadequate.

The only bike/pedestrian ramp up to mass ave is on the northbound side of the street and there is no clear way for people on bikes to get to the southbound bike lanes on Mass ave. from the Dudley White path (or vice versa). Because of this, people do a variety of weird and potentially dangerous things to get there. Please add a crossing here to ensure that people on bikes can head safely in both directions on Mass ave. from these ramps.
Pedestrians are only given TEN seconds to cross this. I walk this to go to work every week and it is NEVER enough time.
Observed bikers on these streets and I was terrified for them. You could tell they were concerned about their safety as well as they are always covered with safety/visibility gear.

People going north on Washington Street turning left on Medford Street often cross the double line early and make unpredictable, fast, and wide-angle turns. I and more than one of my other coworkers who commute by bike into downtown Boston have almost been hit here while we had the right of way in the bus/bike lane. Could the centerline hardening at the Washington/thatcher intersection be continued north a bit?

There is a dangerous combination of different conditions/bad driver behavior on this short stretch of Milk St. The westbound side of the street from Washington to Sewall is CONSTANTLY blocked in the morning by delivery and trade vehicles. And Hawley and Arch street are both blind corners where drivers rarely come to a complete stop before turning onto Milk. As a result, coming east downhill on my bike on Milk, I've almost been hit head on many times on my daily commute by drivers turning left out of those streets into the oncoming traffic lane. People turning out of Hawley and Arch also more generally just don't completely stop unless there are pedestrians directly in front of them in the crosswalk, so I have to stop or dodge to avoid getting hit here at least once a month.
This bike lane has a car in it every time I pass through here.  Please add barriers to block illegal parking, clearly the signs and paint are not enough.

I bike through here regularly and rarely am I able to bike through the whole bike lane without having to merge into traffic because a car is blocking it. This bike lane needs physical barriers to keep the cars out.

The intersection of Charles St and Cambridge St right next to the Charles MGH station is horrendous every single morning. The stoplight schedule needs to be better timed and there should be police directing traffic. People are constantly running red lights, blocking the flow of traffic and in turn causing more traffic. Also the off ramp from Storrow drive into this intersection needs better signage or police presence. People are constantly blocking off the right lane which is meant for going straight onto Charles St. They always stay in the right lane and try to get into the left lane at the last second at the intersection of the off ramp and longfellow bridge. It causes unnecessary built up traffic and impedes pedestrians from safely crossing. Something needs to be done.

This road needs a diet. Folks swerve around idling delivery trucks and try to make the next light. The sidewalks could be bumped out 50% or a protected bike lane could be easily added. Both would do wonders.

The intersection is narrow for the amount of traffic, including of large trucks, it handles. It is exacerbated by the awkward angles at which Tremont, Dartmouth, and West Dedham streets intersect; and by the lack of street markings to help straight versus turning traffic in all directions. At certain times of the day, local school traffic (to the south) and commuter traffic (north-south) ensure that drivers are frustrated by the time they reach this intersection.

The result is frustration by drivers (lack of clear sight, lack of clarity of which cars are going straight versus not), which often leads to speeding and ignoring of yellow and red lights. The "no-turn on red" sign is too often ignored even by local D-4 police. It also leads to far too many near-crashes with pedestrians who are confused or ignorant to the dangerous features of this intersection. The recent Tremont upgrades did little to alleviate issues with this intersection.

While walking or biking from the PDW path to the dam this slip lane is really awful. While walking it makes you have to cross twice, after potentially already waiting quite a while for the light. But on a bike it's genuinely dangerous as there is no clear way you are supposed to get to the bike lane on the dam. You have a walk signal so assume a safe crossing but drivers are coming at you in this slip lane, and they often do not yield.

I ride a bike, on this street as part of my commute sometimes. This bike lane is horrible. It is in the door zone on a very busy road and there are almost always cars in it. This is even worse at night when it is more dangerous to have to merge into traffic.

Cars entering and exiting the garage do not yield to path users far too often. The garage has terrible visibility while exiting and drivers often pull completely into the path before stopping. Drivers entering the garage also often do not yield when turning right into it, specifically to south bound path users. This is worsened by the blue bikes ad stand (keep the station remove the ads) which obscures visibility.

The switch from right side bike lanes to left side bike lanes going East and from left side bike lanes to right side bike lanes going West is awful. If you are really going to make bikes cross two lanes of traffic at a busy intersection on a major street you need to provide both a clear path to do so and signal time as well. The current set up is hostile and dangerous.

The median gap is too small here creating conflicts between pedestrians and people on bikes. either widen the gap or eliminate the median completely and use the freed up space to improve physical separation of the bike lanes.
Cars in the bike lane every time.

Cars routinely blaze right through this stop sign. It's generally not a big deal, as most cyclists are on the left while pedestrians are on the right with little need to cross the street. But sometimes cyclists need to turn right and occasionally I will come from the right side and cross the street on my bike. The Stop sign here is on the right between drivers and parked cars. An additional stop sign (or just moving this one) on the left side of the street would help drivers who simply don't see the stop sign. Though I would guess most drivers simply don't care...

The walk signal is far too short. I'm a fast walker, but it is 100% impossible to get from one side of Commonwealth Ave to the other before the walk signal starts blinking red. For those with a handicap, they would surely have to wait for a second cycle, which can be quite long here.

This intersection is utter chaos for cyclists. To cross Charles Street we have to traverse down Charles Street a bit, then cross, then go backwards and finally back up Boylston Street. 90% I completely forget about the "proper" crossing and simply cross via the pedestrian island. Sure, it's a chaotic intersection but it is unnecessarily chaotic for bikes, especially considering a lot of bikes around here are Blue Bikes.

The movement to get onto the bike lane at the Museum of Science dam (Route 28) is way too dangerous. Near misses from drivers who do not acknowledge the pedestrian crossing lights. The flex posts are mostly gone - probably because they were hit by turning vehicular traffic.

This stretch of roadway is essential for connecting the Paul Dudley White Path to the Somerville Community Path. It is used by commuters and recreational users alike, and Rte 28 imposes unsafe conditions.

Please consider removing this slip lane.

Many, many people turning right, traveling west, from Huntington onto Mass Ave disregard the "no right on red", or don't notice it exists. Oftentimes, cars won't even stop and then turn right, they'll treat it like a slip lane. I run/walk this intersection nearly every day, and have seen many near-misses and twice I've seen pedestrians get hit (thankfully not seriously). Moving the "no right on red" sign from the far side of the intersection (the Symphony Hall side) to the approach side (the Horticultural Society side) could increase visibility.

This intersection is very dangerous. Cars turning from Deforest onto West Street have poor visibility and cars traveling on West Street are often going over the speed limit. Several accidents have occurred at this intersection over the last few years. It is also very hard for pedestrians to cross West Street to access the bus stops on either side of the street with cars going over the speed limit.

Cars going South down Mass Ave turning left onto Commonwealth Ave are pressured to turn even when there are pedestrians or bikers going down Mass Ave. This is because it’s so busy that they have no other opportunity to turn. It’s horribly dangerous, and could really benefit from a protected left or a do-not-turn sign entirely. If anyone spends 5 min observing the intersection at rush hour, they will know exactly what I mean.

When crossing Mass Ave in front of Deuxave, cars turning right are often speeding without yielding to pedestrians. I have had many close calls as someone who uses that intersection every day. Ideally, there should be an all-direction Walk signal so that cars are at a red light the entire time. The entire intersection of Mass Ave and Comm Ave really needs to be re-evaluated.
Drivers turning left often do not yield to pedestrians

There were crosswalks and speed bumps on every street within the West Broadway development. A few years back some of the speed bumps were taken down without any notice to the residents. The streets within the development have been poorly maintained. The crosswalks indicators have faded away over the years and they are in need of repair. The West Broadway development is in need of speed bumps. Due to heavy high speed traffic using the development streets as a cut through from D.st, C & West Seventh, Orton Marotta and Joyce Heyes Way. The housing development is within a school zone, a neighborhood park and community church. The West Broadway Housing development is also apart of a state owned residential home for the severely handicapped and disabled. It has been increasingly dangerous for the children, elderly and disabled residents to cross the streets within the community. There is a desperate need for these concerns to be addressed for the safety and well being for the residents.
This segment is heavily trafficked by bikers and is extremely dangerous as drivers will double park and block the end of the protected bike lane and park all along the curb.

People do not yield to pedestrians. It is a shame that the safety improvements by northeastern that narrow the road are not implemented here. I have been honked at and yelled at by drivers speeding down while I am in the crosswalk getting across the street to my home.
People do not yield here and speed. Why weren't the safety implementations done on the South End portion of Tremont St done here? It is night and day walking here vs in the more narrow area.

Biking to UMass is extremely unsafe on Mt Vernon. People block the bike lane and illegally park even though there are massive parking lots and street parking on the other side for drop off. This is one of the only ways to get to UMass and a lot of staff and students use this route. The bike path needs to be sidewalk level or have concrete barriers. I have almost been hit several times and get cut off by drivers stopping right in front of my and parking.
Very hard to see anything with the curved road and parked cars. Very likely to have car accidents here.

Large number of cars picking up symphony hall goers on mass ave and blocking bike lane causing dangerous conditions and traffic. Symphony hall has a loading/drop-off/pick-up area on the Huntington side that is not used. This is a tragedy waiting to happen and a 72 year old biker was already killed at this intersection last year. please install barriers and prevent another tragedy from happening and advise Symphony Hall to better communicate the area where people can be dropped off and picked up on Huntington Ave. I have almost been hit countless times trying to go around large vehicles causing low visibility situations and I have been attacked by drivers that were angry that I went around a vehicle in the bike lane.

Boston city public buses and local cars run the red light at the intersection of Massachusetts Avenue and Belvidere Street heading northbound, at 150 Massachusetts Ave. The cars accumulate due to traffic and they block the entire pedestrian intersection. 

This puts thousands of college students in danger of head on accidents and pedestrians must walk between cars to cross the blocked intersection.

Please consider painting a "block the box" on the pavement and raising the height of the northbound stop light at this intersection. The intersection is blocked by cars multiple times a day, every day, and it has continued for more than 10 years. Thank you.

The pedestrian intersection at Belvidere Street and Mass Ave is always blocked by cars and buses running the red light. Please increase visibility with a "don't block the box" paint on the pavement, in addition to evaluating the placement of the hard-to-see stoplight. Thank you!

This is a cross walk to the Washington Irving School, which currently serves as upper school (5th & 6th grade) for Sumner but is under renovation and will soon house the fully merged Sumner and Philbrook school, putting much more emphasis on this cross walk. Drivers travel at high speeds along this stretch and additional cross walk signalization and/or traffic calming is needed to make the crossing safe and also protect cyclists in the bike lane here. A teacher was struck a few weeks ago helping kids cross the street and my son is now afraid to cross here.

This neighborhood street is used as a cut-through between Hyde Park Ave and Washington Street and with no signals or stop signs between Blakemore and Firth, this street becomes busy with drivers reaching high speeds. Because of the curve of the street at the entrance to Flaherty Pool and playground, sight lines are decreased for both drivers and pedestrians, making it dangerous for all ages to cross. Traffic calming and speed humps / crossing tables would be appropriate here and at the entrance of Dale Village further east/south on Florence. Lots of kids and elders make use of the pool and playground so the crossing here is the obvious place. My 10 yo son is fully independent to go to the pool for swim practice but is afraid to cross Florence generally.

This is a bus stop for the 30 and 15 buses. It is the only bus stop between Rozzie Square and Hyde Park Ave that does NOT have a cross walk. It is the most convenient bus stop for anyone wanting to access the neighborhood on the north side of the street and frequently would have taken the bus up from Rozzie Square to avoid carrying packages or groceries etc up the hills. Meanwhile, drivers typically come down the hill VERY fast here and give the curve of the road neither driver, nor pedestrian has great sight lines given higher car speeds. A cross walk and signage would help call out that this is a place for crossing.
The cars have a green light at the same time that bikes/ walkers have a walk sign.  I saw a biker just barely avoid getting hit.

Those turning left and right in vehicles do not yield to pedestrians while turning onto Newmarket even though pedestrians have the walk sign and right of way. Very dangerous and stressful for those trying to cross safely.

Please please address the issues at the intersection of Massachusetts Ave. and Belvidere Street (160 Mass Ave). It is very dangerous for pedestrians and bikers due to traffic buildup and drivers running the northbound stoplight.

This is an extremely wide street and is a major corridor for people coming from South Boston (as I do commute every day from there). At some points it is 3 lanes wide and it is never congested. A parking protected bike lane would be extremely beneficial. I have almost been hit multiple times here to get to the Tremont St bike lanes.
Lots of ride share/food delivery drivers park their cars in the bus/bike lane, making cycling dangerous (blocks visibility and increases risk of dooring) and impedes bus traffic.

As a cyclist, I very much appreciate the drastic improvements to bike infrastructure in the city. Also, I see cyclists speeding through this intersection, running red lights, especially when heading south on Mass Ave. The area is densely populated, largely with members of the Berklee community heading toward the various buildings that comprise the school's campus in that area. I believe that if a bicycle light were added to the traffic lights, cyclists would be more likely to stop on red. I know that when I see a bicycle traffic light, I feel seen and respected, and I am therefore encouraged to cooperate with the rules of the system. I believe other cyclists have a similar experience. A colleague of mine was severely injured by a cyclist who ran the red light as he headed south on Mass Ave. I'd like to do everything possible to prevent another incident like this one.

This intersection serves hundreds of pedestrians trying to cross the street all day long. The bike and scooter traffic on Mass Ave has increased tremendously in recent years. Many cyclists think of themselves as pedestrians, and do not stop when the light is red for cars. But the intersection is a 4-way "go" for pedestrians, meaning the bikes and scooters often ride full-speed into crowds of pedestrians crossing their path. Tourists frequent this area, and aren't conditioned to check for bikes before stepping into the street. We have had multiple accidents and near-misses at this intersection.

Bikes need to follow the rules for cars at this intersection. A bike-specific traffic light, timed to match the lights for cars, would send that message.

As a regular bicycle commuter, I greatly appreciate the new bike lanes and use them as often as I can. But double-parked cars make the ride through the Fenway difficult. There are a few "loading zones" available, but I regularly encounter cars in the bike lane in front of take-out spots such as Tatte and Pavement. Cars driving through this area generally will not yield to a bicyclist trying to go around these cars, so the bicyclist ends up trapped until the traffic clears. It is a dangerous situation for the bicyclists.

No exaggeration - I have never had a single driver yield to me while trying to use this crosswalk. I gave up trying to cross here because of people speeding and not yielding. It's an absolute joke. No visibility for pedestrians. Why can't Dot Block fund an improvement here?

Despite the narrow street, amazingly people absolutely FLY down Church Street, and there is barely a sidewalk on either side. Impossible to walk down the street without walking in the middle of the street with cars zooming by. It is a fatality waiting to happen!!!

Massive pothole, can swallow whole tire, reported to Charlestown police twice, been there for a month and getting bigger, completely invisible when coming from Cambridge, car constantly swerve, stop, prone to accidents.

A pedestrian was killed here. Despite the bus stops on both sides this is a dangerous crossing. The cross walk is a double double threat crosswalk, with a safety island too small to really work for multiple people or for bikes, and no light. There is a pedestrian beacon but there is a much brighter electronic billboard to distract drivers from it. The nearest crossings are about half a mile away as the crow flies, and further on foot. Multiple improvements are needed.

A pedestrian was killed here. The city had made improvements to protect the bike lane because they knew this location was dangerous with crossover speeds and aggressive driving behavior. However drivers kept crashing into the barriers and raised a fuss about it. The city seemed to have decided that it would prefer the cars hit people instead of the barriers and now someone is dead. 

You knew this location was dangerous, so you put in protected bike lanes. Then you got more confirmation it was dangerous (the people crashing into the barriers) and rather than make further improvements to enhance safety you undid the improvements and left it in its originally dangerous state. There are consequences to such decisions. Please do not make them again.

Drivers coming off the highway and turning onto Kneeland street don't yield for pedestrians. There have been too many near misses of cars zooming past families walking within the crosswalk. Cars also often drive the wrong way and have multiple times in the past month crossed over the median and knocked over street signs. Street signs of the pedestrian walkway have not been sufficient to prevent accidents and near misses.
Cars don't yield to pedestrians while pedestrians are crossing and often time run red lights as well trying to beat the light adding to the dangerous crossings.
Drivers constantly drive excessively fast and speed down Lincoln St. as if it was an extension of the highway. They fail to yield for pedestrians crossing the street.

People speed down this street and don't yield for pedestrians at this crosswalk. The crosswalk is also a bit faded and is darker so when it's dark out, it's harder to see a pedestrian waiting to cross or even in the middle of the crosswalk.

My wife and I have filed several 311 reports here, and there has been several accidents here prior. 

Crossing from Cornwall onto Peter Parley is very dangerous as a consequence. This is worsened by the reverse happening on the opposite side of the street from Peter Parley Rd to Cornwall as well. 

The very easy solution here is to at make it impossible to park here (which is already a restriction from signage that people ignore) with cones like they have on the parallel street (which is far less risky), Amory Street.

My wife and I have filed several 311 reports here, and there has been several accidents here prior. 

Crossing from Peter Parley onto Washington or Cornwall is very dangerous as a consequence. This is worsened by the reverse happening on the opposite side of the street from Cornwall to Peter Parley Rd as well. 

The very easy solution here is to at make it impossible to park here (which is already a restriction from signage that people ignore) with cones like they have on the parallel street (which is far less risky), Amory Street.

The crash map data is missing several accidents. We have photos of likely 6-8 accidents that have happened here over the last 2 years. At times they are collisions between two driving vehicles. Folks have missed recognizing the stop sign. Others are simply speeding. Many times we've seen accidents where someone simply smacks into a parked car. This is simply a dangerous intersection which so happens to be near a neighborhood school just up the street. I hate speed bumps, but a speed bump would help the safety of this whole neighborhood tremendously here.
People speed through this area.
Almost got hit today while crossing the pedestrian walkway due to a car being illegally parked blocking the driver's vision.

Cars speed on this. As a pedestrian, despite being in the crosswalk, folks do not stop to yield to the pedestrian unless they were already being considerate enough to drive the speed limit. 

This is exacerbated by the illegally parked car blocking the  blocking this intersection so oncoming traffic has a harder chance seeing pedestrians soon enough to stop comfortably so they're incentivized to blitz on by. 

It's only a matter of time before either another car accident happens or a pedestrian gets hit at this intersection : (
Another instance of an illegally parked car, this time in emergency parking. Makes it dangerous for pedestrians and vehicles entering intersection

properties.request_other: Illegally parked cars make this intersection extremely dangerous for both pedestrians and drivers
properties.comments:
Illegally parked cars make this intersection extremely dangerous for both pedestrians and drivers.

Daily occurrences of illegally parked cars here make this an extremely dangerous intersection for both pedestrians and drivers. It obscures visibility for cross traffic from Peter Parley <--> Cornwall and makes it very difficult for pedestrians to cross safely across washington, or even to continue on washington as intersecting washington traffic (turning off of washington) has low visibility into pedestrians.

The crosswalk at this intersection is so faded that cars do not see it, and do not stop. Pedestrian traffic at this intersection is very heavy due to students at Berklee crossing to access campus buildings on Hemenway Street.
Bikes need their own traffic light at this intersection. We have near-misses with pedestrians on a daily basis.
Illegally parked car to the left makes it impossible to see to take a left without risking being t-boned.

Electronic billboards are proven through several studies to distract divers and make crashes near them more deadly and dangerous. A pedestrian was recently killed in this intersection below such a billboard. There is no stop light for the pedestrian crossing, which is only marked by a sign and flashing lights. 

It is very likely that this bright billboard reduces the visibility of this crossing, and draws drivers attention away from any pedestrians in it. Please remove it in addition to improving the crossing.

It is unacceptable that a vision zero community maintains digital advertising along roadways. Please remove this digital billboard and consider adopting an outdoor ad free zone in Boston, as Lexington, Lincoln, and Concord already have.

properties.request_other: Drivers do not stop for pedestrians at crosswalk
properties.comments: Always have to wait until streets are completely clear to walk since drivers rarely stop for pedestrians at this crosswalk. This is a common occurrence. However, just had my first incident where a driver was inches away from hitting me and my dog as I started to cross the crosswalk, where I’d once again had just been waiting at for the cars to clear since no one stopped. I had to stop mid-crossing so that the driver had enough time to hard brake for us
Busy area. Car was speeding from and could have hit us walking across the street. There needs to be lights or something to make this a safer place for pedestrians.

Cars are constantly speeding, running stop signs and never respecting pedestrians . There’s a school on Peter parley and they use this intersection to go to the park. Please take our requests seriously and make this intersection safer for our neighborhood. Add lights and speed bumps.
Drivers speed and do not stop for pedestrians. Add lights or speed bumps to ensure this is a safe crosswalk.
Cars do not stop for pedestrians
residents and patrons of the area feel that it's unsafe to cross in the crosswalk due to cars not stopping for pedestrians. suggestions include: better lighting, raised crosswalks.

bus stop across the street from 612 blue - pedestrians get off the bus and immediately cross the street outside of the crosswalk while cars are going too fast. better signage or design to funnel pedestrians to the crosswalk is needed.

clancy road is a cut through from gallivan to washington and vice versa. cars reach up to 50 miles per hour on this street to avoid the red light. speed humps would make cars slow down. this street abuts a public playground where many families are crossing the street to use the playground.

The painting on the crosswalk is so faded it is very hard for drivers to see. Also there are no signs warning of the upcoming crosswalk. As a result cars frequently drive through the crosswalk and don't stop for pedestrians. Finally, cars frequently park in the crosswalk outside Starbucks blocking access to the ramp
This intersection is missing pedestrian signals for some of the crossings.

Excessive speed on this stretch of Lamartine Street where many families live and walk to school, nearby playgrounds, and the train.  There are not enough crosswalks and no calming measures.  Cars travel upwards of 50 mph.  There is also no marked center lane and it is two way traffic at high speeds.  Dangerous for drivers and pedestrians
Drivers turning on and off of Congress St at Sleeper St can be very aggressive and impatient. Whenever I am walking along Congress St there, it is very common for drivers to not yield to me.
it's very common for cars to drive into the crosswalk before proceeding onto Congress St. I frequently have to wave down cars to make them aware that I'm there when I'm walking east on Congress St.""

A child was killed here. directly in front of the children's museum. This should never be allowed to happen again. You can prevent it forever by blocking this block to through traffic. Create a pocket park and name it in honor of the girl who died. Maintain loading access by maintaining the street connections to the alley and maintain pedestrian and accessible rolling connections only through the block abutting congress.

The sidewalks here are too narrow. When people are waiting outside here for help and treatment the sidewalk gets too full spilling into the street. This gives reckless drivers opportunity to exercise social stigma through reckless, threatening, and potentially violent driving. Expand the side walks.

There are people crossing here whether or not the city recognizes their humanity. This is a crazy dangerous intersection right next to such a concentration of services. People cross here all the time. It is nowhere near safe enough and people drive aggressively here often. Bike paths also lead into here now and there is even more non vehicular movement through this incredibly automobile oriented intersection.
Bike lanes in JP centre are door zone and the paint is extremely faded. They need refreshing and at that point they should be more generally improved.
this intersection is too big to cross in one cycle, only lasts about 15 seconds
the train tracks are incredibly uneven and make it very difficult to drive across in one light cycle, backing up traffic down narrow Allston Street

Harvard Ave from Comm Ave to Cambridge street is always backed up because delivery drivers are constantly double parking their cars on both sides of the street, meaning cars are always crossing into the other direction's traffic, bike lanes are constantly blocked so they have to go into the street, and it's very difficult to see pedestrians in the crosswalks

delivery drivers are constantly double parking their cars in the BUS/BIKE only lane (which is very clearly marked the entire length of the street but cars driving thru also don't follow the rules), constantly causing traffic because the busses and the bikes have to merge into the thru traffic lane to get around. this happens on both sides of street all the time
bike lane visibility is low - drivers have trouble telling that bike lane exists, Please restripe and/or add green paint to delineate better

This intersection is super dangerous. A bicyclist was hit and run by a truck driver in it yesterday. This intersection needs protected intersection treatments and both Charles and Cambridge need protected bike lanes.
There is no official way to get from the ramps to the south/east bound bike lane so people do all kinds of crazy things to get there.

While this project will, once completed, massively improve the bike paths along mass ave the current set up during construction is terrible forcing bikes to merge into traffic with no leading interval from far to drivers right side. The road surface there is also terrible making  this worse. There need to be provisions for bike paths during construction like there are for streets and sidewalks.
This is a blind crossing for bikes headed northeast and cars headed east. Cars frequently do not yield in the crosswalk.
People regularly drive the wrong way down this one way and Google maps directs people to do so.

I bike this way to avoid biking around the pond like I am supposed to (bikes should be allowed around the pond as long as they yield to pedestrians) but the city does not encourage this behavior. This bike lane is narrow and unmarked. Drivers seem to think it is a shoulder and regularly drive in it. It needs marking and physical protection.
Bikes should be allowed around the pond it is much safer than the current alternatives.

A white service van turned right from Longwood Ave onto Avenue Louis Pasteur and did not see me on my bike in spite of my fluoro yellow reflector vest and bike lights. Luckily I was biking slowly enough that I was able to turn with the van and not get hit. Cars often don't yield to pedestrians in this area of Longwood Ave either.

I was going straight on Longwood Ave at Brookline Ave towards Riverway when two SUVs in a row tried to turn left from Longwood Ave onto Brookline Ave. They tried to turn right after a car went straight just in front of me and failed to yield to me continuing straight. They didn't see me in spite of my fluoro yellow reflector vest and front and rear bike lights that were on. It was about 5 pm on Tuesday, May 14, 2024 and cloudy but still daylight. I had to yell out to the SUVs to get them to stop turning. There needs to be bike-specific infrastructure here. Paint and sharrows are not enough. Cars need to have a left turn signal separate from oncoming traffic because drivers get so impatient when tryin to make a left turn that they barely look when they think they see an opening to turn. This is the most stressful and scary part of my commute to work biking from Porter Square in Cambridge.

It's very difficult to cross Riverway on Longwood Ave by bike especially going towards the Longwood Medical Area as there is no protected bike lane so to go straight across, you need to cross traffic into the left lane because the right lane is a right only car lane.
Vehicles are blocking the bike lane in front of the restaurants here every time I bike commute to work at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, forcing cyclists into the traffic lane.
another scary intersection on Longwood Ave to travel through on a bike because cars and vehicles turning left don't always yield or even look for bicycle traffic.

Paint is not protection. There's a partial painted bike lane, but otherwise zero bike infrastructure and it's extremely harrowing to bike through. Cyclists often bike through the intersection during the 4-way walk signal to get ahead of traffic, and they yield to pedestrians, but this is problematic because of the number of pedestrians crossing in all directions.
need protected bike lanes on Longwood Ave because cars block them or pass through the partial painted lane all the time.
need bike-specific infrastructure and protection approaching the intersection of Longwood Ave and Binney St. Sharrows are ignored and don't help visibility of cyclists.
Need bike-specific infrastructure and protection at Longwood Ave and Blackfan. Busy intersection with cars turning into Children's Hospital.
Bike lane disappears at this end of Longwood Ave and is very much needed for protection and visibility of cyclists on this very busy stretch of road.

Cars are consistently running the red light when traveling north, posing a hazard to peds and cyclists who have a green light. Cars traveling south do not stop at the stop sign, posing a double threat to peds and cyclists. There should be increased enforcement until permanent changes can be made.
There is no bike lane here and fast-moving cars make for a very scary ride. Given its connection to SW Corridor, it sees heavy bicycle traffic but is not built for it.

The light timing and multiple crossings all along this connection between the Fens and the Greenway are ridiculous. Pedestrians get stranded in high speed traffic islands if and when the lights ever change. All of these intersections should be scramble crossings.

The unprotected bike lane always has double parked cars or delivery trucks in it. There are dozens of motorcycles that also use this bike lane, which is frightening as a cyclist. The entirety of Mass Ave is unpleasant and scary for biking.

I am a resident who lives on this corner (504 Beacon St). There is a right turn lane to get off of the Mass Ave bridge onto beacon street with a no right turn on red sign and a traffic signal for the right turn lane. I frequently notice people who honk at cars in front of them and then speed around the cars to make an illegal right turn on red. This happens all of the time.
Could speed humps/ other traffic calming measures be put on Lincoln Street? This street is super straight and encourages speeding, so some sort of traffic calming measure would be really appreciated

The eastern side of the intersection of Allston St and Brighton Ave needs a crosswalk. I see people dashing across the street, away from the crosswalk, to avoid having to wait for the whole light cycle to get the walk signal again

Even with the recent redesign, I don't feel safe crossing the crosswalk here. Cars rarely yield to me, and I've even see a rear-end crash occur because I tried to cross. One of the RRFB signals was destroyed at this location as well
The sidewalks over the MBTA rails are in terrible shape, it all feels like a big tripping hazard
Vehicles do not yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk
Speeding vehicles, near the boys and girls club, are a concern to me. Are speed cushions an option here?

This crosswalk to cross Peter Parley is exceptionally long because of the way the sidewalks curve away. Because of parked cars, as a pedestrian you can't see cars driving down the hill until you're out in the street. In addition, since PP Rd is only wide enough for one lane of traffic (but it's a 2 way street), Cars are often focused on each other (rather than looking for pedestrians) and they often swerve into the crosswalk space in order to make way for a car going the other direction. They can't see you (pedestrian) and you can't see them. 

This is the crossing that stresses me out as a parent (when walking with my kids or when thinking about allowing them to walk on their own). 

Possible solutions: 
Bumping the sidewalks out
making Peter Parley one way
creating a parking-free zone around the crosswalk
This sidewalk is terrible! Mud and ice are bad, and it's really hard to navigate with a stroller or scooter. Also, cars entering the garage add a hazard (could the entrance/exit be made smaller?)
The wait for the walk signal is ridiculously long and it encourages pedestrians to walk without waiting for it. Sometimes cars have a red light but the walk still doesn't go.
Cars illegally turn right on red. One of these days they will get hit by a car coming down Montebello.
no curb cuts

It is absurd to have nothing but a crosswalk here. We need a light!! This road feels like a highway to the cars, and yet it's a common crossing where kids and families cross to access their park!! We have been asking for this for years!!
This is such a miss! The bike path just ends here with no easy way to navigate the intersections, no way to connect to the SW Corridor, etc.

Crossing from Price Road onto Glenville Ave as a pedestrian can be tricky. Could a curb extension be put in so the crossing has improved visibility? If not, could speed humps be installed to slow down oncoming cars

We live at that location and cars go too fast (over speed limit) up and down street. There is also limited visibility because of curve. There have been several vehicle accidents and last year a pedestrian was struck and injured by speeding car. First responders came.
If they put a speed hub just before the curve at 42 Newton St. call and after the curve at 60 Newton st it would slow the rate of speeds safely. 
Many cars race through the neighborhood to cut through to avoid tragic and have hit vehicles, a pedestrian was struck, and people’s animals have been hit

Exiting this intersection going south, as the road shifts left, cars & trucks regularly cut through the bike lane, causing cyclists to be "squeezed" as the cars drive by.  This can be especially dangerous with large trucks, as there is a real risk of being run over.  

There were once white pylons here which I found were effective at keeping cyclists and automobiles separated at this squeeze, however they were removed some time ago.  

As a personal anecdote, I've seen 3 near misses at this intersection over the past year.  It's only a matter of time before a serious incident occurs here.

Drivers constantly run this 4-way stop. It's so dangerous - I routinely almost get hit by cars when I'm in the crosswalk here, because they're impatient, they try to beat the pedestrian across the street, or they are looking down at their phones. I would guess 98% of drivers don't come to a full stop here or yield to pedestrians. The crosswalk paint and stop line paint on the north crossing is totally worn off, too.
Bad stretch of potholes on Day Street next to the MSPCA. I am always bracing for a flat tire when I bike.

People absolutely gun it up and down Bynner St, only to come to a screeching halt at the red light or run the stop sign at Bynner & Day. There were just two car accidents at Bynner & Day within the span of 10 days. I live on Bynner and hear cars tearing down the street at 40+ mph all day long.

This is a popular place to cross for pedestrians accessing the staircase outside the Cultural Center for trips between Shaw's and the bus stop on Meridian and Lexington or further into Eagle Hill. There is no crosswalk, and parked cars severely limit visibility. Please look into adding a crosswalk here and daylighting either side of the street.
The bike lane is incredibly faded on this stretch of Maverick Street. Cars often drive or park in the bike lane, likely because they cannot see there is one there

Cars often do not yield at this intersection, and sometimes are going above the speed limit. Many pedestrians use this crosswalk to access the EB Greenway, and especially the adjacent dog park. Please consider installing a stop sign here.
This carriageway runs beside the Arborway. People flagrantly break the speed limit to beat the traffic on the actual Arborway.
a crosswalk or street here would be great!

Bikers going toward Forest Hills Station across the slip lane turning onto South Street from Arborway have a green light at the same time as Drivers using the slip lane. Effectively, both have the right of way. It's only a matter of time before someone gets killed here.
This is a critical biking corridor from Dorchester/Southie into the city. People drive very fast here, and there are often cars parked in the right lane.

There's no bike lane from Arlington to Southie. Maps suggests following Herald St and Washington St, but people drive very aggressively on Herald St and it's hard to make a left turn on Washington St.
Lots of people cross to Enterprise St here where there is no crosswalk. The road is wide and drivers go fast. Narrowing street and providing a crosswalk would really improve safety.

Please put a crosswalk from the corner of Willow Court across Allstate Road directly to where the sidewalk goes through the parking lot. A speed hump/table would be even better, since drivers routinely speed along this straight section. The parking lot here is in general very unfriendly to pedestrians and it would be great if the city could make it safer and more convenient to walk through.

I hope the bike lane will be extended further up Berkeley. At the light, bikers going straight who were in the right lane are suddenly in the way of traffic turning right on the green arrow. The surface is also super rough here which makes it hard to steer with one hand to give turn signals.

Baker Street from Catholic Memorial across Spring Street (when the light is Green) to its intersection with Centre Street has become the “work-around” to bypass the “congestion” caused by Boston’s safety initiative to reduce the traffic lanes in West Roxbury Centre for traffic in both directions between South Brookline and Dedham.
    Speed Humps-not bumps-should installed from adjacent to the school crossing at Catholic Memorial down Baker Street (at least 2) to Ansonia Road. Two stop signs should installed on Baker Street on either side of its intersection with Ansonia Road adjacent to the crosswalk along with one speed hump on the slope on Baker Street adjacent to the Kilmer School.

The combined green walk signal and flashing hand countdown only provides enough time for pedestrians to cross half the street before turning to the solid red hand. Drivers will NOT yield for pedestrians already in the crosswalk, especially after seeing the red hand for pedestrians. The green walk pedestrian interval should last just as long as the green signal for vehicles.
Most drivers do not yield for pedestrians at this crosswalk

This intersection feels chronically dangerous as a pedestrian. Right- and left-turning drivers (especially turning from Albany onto Mass Ave) routinely choose not to yield to pedestrians who have the walk light and are already in the middle of the crosswalk.

There is no bike infrastructure on Longwood Ave and this intersection with Riverway is particularly bad. Bikes typically go through the intersection with the 4-way pedestrian signal to avoid being invisible when vehicles are turning, especially with large vans and trucks that further block visibility. This is not ideal, even if cyclists yield to pedestrians. During morning rush hour, when cars on Riverway have a green arrow to turn left onto Longwood, they are not yielding to pedestrians/cyclists crossing because they are only concerned with the fact that they have a green arrow and there is traffic stopped around the intersection that they want to get through.

Vehicle drivers speed through the intersection trying to make the light. This is especially problematic when drivers are trying to turn left. They will accelerate hard to try and make the turn before the light changes.
Vehicle drivers go through the red light from all directions because they get tired of waiting for the light and are impatient.
the roadway surface has potholes and uneven pavement in areas. This is a nuisance for vehicle drivers, but dangerous for cyclists whose wheels can get caught in uneven pavement and cause a crash.
The crosswalk time is relatively short considering it's a 4-way walk signal and there are multiple lanes to cross.

This is a large area for pedestrians to cross with multiple lanes in all directions. Adding bike infrastructure and shorter crosswalks would make a huge difference for cyclists' and pedestrians' safety and their visibility to drivers.

Most cars do not stop when the flashing lights on the RRFBs are activated.  

Even more dangerous, if one lane of traffic does stop and a pedestrian begins to cross the road, they may be blocked from the view of a second lane of traffic, leading to the potential for a fatal accident – a “double threat” that the Boston Transportation Department calls a fundamentally dangerous design. 

One of our neighbors was an eye-witness to a crash that occurred for this reason several years ago. And in 2018, another neighbor was walking while pushing her child in a stroller in the crosswalk of the Westchester/Centre Street intersection when a speeding vehicle in the second lane of traffic approached and nicked the stroller.  Fortunately, no one was physically hurt in these cases, but these accidents and near-accidents are incredibly traumatizing on an emotional level, and those involved may not be so fortunate next time.
People often speed down this street at night. Sometimes going upwards up 50 miles an hour. Maybe a speed trap or camera to capture license plates (for tickets) would help cut down on this problem.

Trying to cross  at this intersection is very dangerous. There is no light, or any kind of walk signal, that would alert cars to actually stop for pedestrians. It is a very frequented place where people, dogs, kids cross the street and cars do not stop when you are in the walkway. There are a lot of "near misses" and people have been hit in this intersection. Pedestrians need to worry about cars turning onto center street, along with cars going in either direction of center street. I am advocating for a blinking "walk light" that can be pushed, similar to how the arboretum has, on the way to Faulkner Hospital.

The bike lane that exists here is incredibly dangerous as cars will continue right towards Forest Hills regardless of if you are needing to head straight toward Soldier's Monument / the Loring-Greenough House. This is also dangerous in a car, but far worse on a bicycle.
The sidewalk in front of 8 Rambler Rd has been broken for multiple years now and is a serious tripping hazard.
This is a street that people speed on, particularly at night. Either coming from Center or coming from the Jamaica way. High speeds are noted.

properties.request_other: This intersection needs a Walk light that pedestrians can push
properties.comments:
This is a very dangerous intersection for pedestrians/bikers, etc trying to cross the street. It is a very frequented cross walk in this neighborhood. Cars often times do not stop for pedestrians in the cross walk or if one side does, the other side just flies by while you are in the middle of the street. If a bus is stopped, cars go around the bus, so it is also hard to cross as a pedestrian with children or dogs. There really needs to be a light that can be pushed to alert people to STOP. Flashing lights and/or a pedestrian signal would be ideal. 
I have witnessed many people almost getting hit.

This is technically an unmarked intersection where Holbrook St meets Centre St. For all residents who live on Holbrook, Dunster, and Dane in this neighborhood, the only way to walk south towards many community landmarks (Curtis Hall, Loring Greenough, JP library, businesses on South St, Forest Hills T), the fastest way to cross is here. The only other routes that use a traffic lights to cross, are to go out of the way 2 blocks in the opposite direction, west, or a block north to the Eliot St intersection. This is not only an issue for people with mobility issues, it’s not good city planning design. Many residents end up just crossing here at this intersection to head to South St, but the street width is about 4 lanes wide, there is no painted crosswalk, and vehicles commonly gas it here because it’s so wide. Residents who come from these 3 streets and beyond need traffic lights and a painted crosswalk here.

I regularly see drivers honk and speed up when BU students are walking here. It's not just that they speed, it's that they try to intimidate pedestrians by endangering them. Speed tables would be appropriate here.

It's a wide crosswalk, and cars always speed, don't yield, and it's right by several parks. It's a dangerous crosswalk, as evidenced by several past pedestrian crashes, and my own personal experience walking there every day.

properties.request_other: Traffic is not stopped for peds
properties.comments: There is a walk signal here, that has no immediately associated traffic light and this causes close calls with cars that don't realize they should stop and pedestrians that have a walk signal frequently.

The Greenway bans bikes and other forms of micro mobility devices, with no exception for use as a mobility aid, however the surrounding streets are not safe to bike on. This policy needs to be reversed.
Charles street is a huge gap in the bike network. Fix it.

Driver behavior is insane on this intersection. There is a separate signal for cars making right turns from Sudbury into Congress so pedestrians can cross safely, yet almost *every* *singe* *time* drivers either try to aggressively cut off pedestrians or if the car at the front of the lane actually obeys the red arrow, the cars behind them will honk incessantly and try to go around them almost crashing into pedestrians despite the red signal. With the city's and police departments apparent zero enforcement policy, safety improvements like protected turns are completely meaningless.

This is a key route that connects residents of the North End to North Station as well as many tourists/concertgoers going to Regina's. The driver behavior at this intersection and nearby intersections is completely unhinged with extremely aggressive speeding, driving in the bus lane, double parking, driving on the wrong side of the road, running red lights and making illegal turns. I think a strict 1 hour enforcement session on this block would probably net about 200 tickets. 
A big issue is people turning into Thacher make the turn without checking for pedestrians (who don't have a signal at all) and aggressively try to cut people off. Just past Thacher is the left turn into Medford St where drivers will block the whole road to make a turn that they could do further up at the light.
Finally, despite the huge ped volume, the light has a beg button and I see confused tourists wondering why they don't get a green light.
There is probably something wrong with this light because it will sometimes skip the pedestrian 'green' cycle even if I pushed the button and a full cycle for traffic in each direction has passed.

Cars are CONSTANTLY speeding on Dorchester Ave down in the Ashmont area. There aren't even any signs on Dorchester Ave stating what the speed limit is!

Additionally, it has become almost impossible to cross the street. Cars don't stop for people who are in crosswalks. People are almost hit by cars while in crosswalks far too frequently in this area - I have witnessed people actively walking in a crosswalk and cars still won't stop. It's only a matter of time before this area adds to the statistics that Vision Zero is trying to eliminate.

Not only is speeding a problem in this area, but drivers constantly run red lights. While walking, I've had the walk signal turn on to cross the street, and have had multiple cars run red lights well after the light had turned red (and well after I've started walking across the street). This area of Dorchester Ave is really dangerous when it comes to how the cars drive.

Cars and large trucks often park on Lincoln very close to Antwerp, blocking the view of oncoming traffic in either or both directions. Now that there's an increase in eastbound traffic it's even more dangerous to try to exit Antwerp. A light or stop signs on Lincoln would be great but at the very least blocking out the spaces for sightlines would help.
This area has a lot of food traffic but drivers insist on treating it like a highway. Cars are constantly flying down this street with no BPD enforcement whatsoever.

Speeding is a problem here. I've witnessed cars that have had to be going 70+ MPH on this road. Just last week, I witnessed 2 very serious car crashes within about a mile of each other on this same road.

This pedestrian crosswalk is used extremely frequently by Wentworth students walking to/from classes. The crosswalk is pedestrian-priority, and even has special markings to indicate so, but drivers don't always yield, and often drive uncomfortably fast. This location is a perfect candidate for a raised crosswalk, which would make crossing the street here much safer.
The lights are too short for people to cross from one side of Huntington avenue to the other without getting stuck on the Green line tracks
No curb cuts. Makes it hard to dock bluebikes at the station

The SW direction on Beacon St, from Park Drive to Carlton St has a dedicated bike lane. Despite heavy bike traffic, this remains a dangerous area for cyclists. (1) Drivers pull into the bike lane at the start and end of the blocks, blocking cyclists from entering the bike lane after crossing Park Drive, or exiting the bike lane (by St. Mary's or Carlton St). (2) Drivers disregard the bike lane markings when parking and pull into the bike lane adjacent to the parking spaces. Subsequently, cars parked over the line regularly have passengers blindly swing doors open. (3) Mopeds regularly park in the bike lane. 

As a cyclist who traverses this road daily, I have close encounters with almost getting doored or having to circumnavigate a car most days of the week, often several times within the same day. Today, as a pedestrian, I was witness to a cyclist getting doored by a rideshare drop-off passenger. He walked off the scrapes and bruises, but the dangers of this section remain.

Make-shift bike lane (paint) suddenly ends on north side of stroad and cyclists/pedestrians are not given a safe path to connect to adjacent sidewalks or the Dudley Path. The sidewalk under the I-90 bridge at North Beacon and Leo Birmingham Pkwy suddenly ends and does not connect to Parsons St. There is a track clearly walked/biked into dirt along the stroad where many people have used. This is unsafe and vehicular traffic have zero regards for pedestrian safety in this area!
The slip-lane on Brighton Ave east bound is a dangerous blind spot for pedestrians where right turning traffic do not slow before the turn.

There needs to be a refuge point here. Pedestrians must cross 4 lanes and are often disregarded from right-turning traffic in the make-shift slip lane and double parkers. A leading pedestrian interval (LPI) can help increase visibility of pedestrians intending to cross.

The ""sidewalk"" between Storrow Dr and Charles River are incredibly narrow in this area and cannot safely accomodate two-way foot traffic. This is a common commuter path where cyclists and pedestrians collide. The sharp guard rail stanchions are a safety hazard while biking at night where people are blinded by oncoming traffic and running into them.
Cyclists are constantly thrown in and out of the make-shift bikes lanes (paint) which is unpredictable and unsafe when traffic is attempting to overtake.
bridge is narrow and pavement is rough, very scary on a bike both north and southbound
Please divide the bike lane into two lanes all around the garden/common. Many people bike the wrong direction and it would be safer if they were just given a designated lane

properties.request_other: the crosswalk is usually blocked by cars when the walk sign is on
properties.comments: I bike daily to work along the Charles river path. Most of the time (4/5 days per week), the crosswalk is blocked by traffic when the walk sign turns on. As a result, pedestrians and cyclists typically have to weave between several lanes of cars to get across the road. It is not uncommon for the crosswalk to be blocked by a large truck, which makes this even more scary. This is a seriously dangerous intersection for pedestrians and should be fixed ASAP before someone gets hurt.

properties.request_other: people perpetually block the crosswalks in this intersection during rush hour
properties.comments: While the recent infrastructure improvements have made an improvement to this intersection, it is still stressful and dangerous to navigate outside a car.  Northbound traffic on Mass Ave (including those turning right from Boylston to Mass Ave) regularly block the crosswalk, causing pedestrians and cyclists to dangerously weave between cars. I think regular enforcement of blocking the intersection here would be very helpful.

given how busy this intersection is with Northeastern students, there absolutely needs to be more time to cross the street. I basically have to run to make it across in one go. On top of that, the light cycle time is way too long.

Drivers frequently do not yield to pedestrians in this crossing. There is a leading pedestrian interval which helps if people are crossing from the MFA side but not from the other side as cars will already be turning by the time you reach it. 

I was almost hit yesterday by a driver who refused to yield to multiple people in the crosswalk, who flipped us off and screamed he had a green light. Please consider replacing the green light with a flashing yellow to encourage yielding to pedestrians or preferably fully separating the pedestrian phase.

Frequently see cars running red lights heading Eastbound on Commonwealth for the right turn onto MA 2. 

Almost right hooked by a vehicle this morning during rush hour. Closest call I've had in 6 months.
Very rough pavement and no protection from speeding cars. People often park in the bike lane as well.
There are always multiple double parked vehicles when I bike through here in the morning.
Very dangerous stretch inbound

properties.request_other: Drivers do not respect No U-Turn sign
properties.comments:
I thank the City for responding to my earlier report regarding the visibility of the “No U-Turn” sign at Castlegate Road and Blue Hill Avenue in Dorchester. I appreciate the city's effort in pruning the tree that had been obstructing the sign.

However, since the initial corrective action, I’ve continued to observe frequent illegal turns at the intersection. 

To address this 

1. **Full Removal of the Tree** – This would eliminate partial obstruction.
2. **Enhanced Pavement Markings** – Add “NO U-TURN” or directional arrows on the road surface to reinforce the sign.
3. **Supplemental Signage** – Consider adding an overhead or mirrored “No U- Turn” sign.
4. **Targeted Enforcement or Data Collection** – A short monitoring period could provide clarity on violation frequency.
5. **Design Modification** – Consider low-cost channelization (e.g., flexible bollards or curb extensions) to physically discourage the turn.

Hello, I've been walking from North Station to Beacon Hill for 3 years, and previously walked from Charles Street Station to Beacon Hill for several years. To get to work, I have to cross both Bowdoin St and Cambridge St at that intersection. There is only about 10 seconds allotted for pedestrians during the walk signal, which applies to all of the crosswalks at the same time. That is barely enough time to cross one street, let alone both. As a result, pedestrians often get caught in the middle of the street as the light is changing, or take the risk to cross the street when traffic is moving in that direction but when there is a break in cars turning. Given how many people commute by foot in this area, I think it would be great if the City considered adding 10 more seconds to the signal so pedestrians can safely get across the street without running or taking any unnecessary risks, which is more in line with other signals on Cambridge St.

intersection at Soldier Monument on Centre Street & South Street needs a traffic light to allow vehicles to turn left or right. And Parking around The Monument inhibits drivers from seeing oncoming traffic.
People speed and don't yield to pedestrians at the pedestrian crossing
People speed and don't yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk
Bike lanes need new flex posts - drivers blocking lanes
The crosswalk at LaGrange St and Westmount Ave in West Roxbury is an accident waiting to happen for a pedestrian. Cars speed through and do not stop. The city is well aware of this issue.

just such a dangerous intersection. cars race in front of pedestrians trying to get the bus stop, trader joes, the library, etc. this intersection needs to change and slow down cars.
I have been yelled at by drivers when crossing Arborway N/S with a ""walk"" sign. Drivers will not yield to pedestrians and cyclists using the crosswalk.

I walk and almost a bike hit me and my dog , it was next to me 3 feet when the teen riding the gas scooter at 40 miles/ hours

It is very hard for cars to see when they are turning onto Corey Road from Bellvista Road, particularly from the north but also from the south if a vehicle is pulled over on the eastbound side of Corey. Cars also often drive far too fast on Corey, particularly downhill on either side of Summit St. I live at this corner and there are accidents all the time, and just now there was a serious one - a car flipped over onto a parked car after being clipped by a turning car whose driver had an obstructed view. It’s a danger not just to drivers but to residents, and this neighborhood has many small children. I think this should be a 4-way stop.

Almost all drivers coming down Webster St approaching Orleans St take a right turn onto Orleans. The traffic on Orleans has no stop sign, and many drivers coming down Webster get fixated looking left and roll into the intersection as they turn right without looking for pedestrians or coming to a stop.

I’ve watched a couple dozen close calls and have had quite a for myself and my dogs as a pedestrian. What’s particularly frightening is that the drivers rolling through the stop sign often don’t even seem to realize they came just a couple feet from hitting a pedestrian and continue their turn without every looking to the right.

I don’t know if a four-way stop would help here, or if something else would be a better solution, but it’s hard to imagine someone won’t get hit at some point if something doesn’t change, especially as ride-share traffic picks up from the Tall Ship

Nearly impossible to see cyclists in the bike lane while I’m taking a right turn at a green light. The cars parked on the side of the road lead to little or no visibility of who or what is in the bike lane.
People turn right from Oak Square onto Faneuil without stopping, slowing down, or looking for pedestrians.

Cars use Nonantum St as a cut through to get to Oak Square from Waverly St. Many go WAY too fast down the street. This is especially dangerous with pedestrians crossing the street to get to and from the Rev. James J Murphy path that leads to the 57/501/503 bus stops.

Cars come flying down Faneuil Street between Parsons St & Oak Square way above the speed limit, ignoring the cross walks and the low-visibility turns from side streets.  Mitigated during rush hour by traffic volumes, but especially dangerous during business hours, evenings, and weekends.

With a blinking yellow and periodic red light at this intersection, I and my neighbors continually witness:
• Vehicles proceeding through red lights on Centre Street
• Confusion regarding left-turn procedures from Louders Lane
• Drivers unsure who has the legal right of way
• Vehicles ignoring flashing pedestrian signals nearby
• Delayed or inconsistent signal changes, especially on weekends
• Concerns involving pedestrians, cyclists, families, and school children

My concerns have increased with a recent incident in which my neighbor's vehicle was struck by another going through the red light, while he had the right of way exiting Louders Lane onto Centre Street. His car was totaled, but thankfully did not experience serious injuries.

This intersection, and many others along Meridian St., and specially those organized along  acute and/or obtuse angles and geometries (`triangle intersections') are hard for drivers to navigate and require strained head turning and bad visibility. Maybe some type of geometry changes, corner parking elimination, curb extensions, might help and also create new public spaces there (increase the ROW real-estate for pedestrians and adjacent businesses), whilst helping drivers in navigating safer intersection for crossing and merging traffic. e.g., perpendicular intersections there and/or off-sets

people often drive at high speeds along this street, Border st., and feels unsafe for pedestrians and bicyclists. The street seems to wide for its purpose and might benefit form some dieting, and perhaps new bike lane, buffered or on sidewalk, linking Central Square with the highly used Lopresti park. Also, mid-block crossings might be very effective in elongated blocks in East Boston, like those found along Border and other streets there. Start with improving conditions for pedestrians, midblock crossings, then worry about bicycle facilities (that seems to be a political hot topic here).

properties.request_other: very confusing intersection and access/egress to/from Maverick Square  for pedestrians and bicyclists.
properties.comments: Unclear pathways into and out from the Square. The entire Square should be redesigned with pedestrians in mind so as to function as a real 'Square', and realign re-accommodate bus feeder routes to be less disruptive of communal space and of pedestrians and bicyclists flow; whilst still functioning as a key transit hub for the city. This is essentially an urban design problem, and thinking 'outside the box' is needed, including repositioning bus access routes and stops along perpendicular local roads to the West of the Square....among other changes that will require coordination and dialogue with MBTA. The city needs to adopt a modal hierarchy policy: pedestrians --> transit --> automobiles. The changes in bus feeder routes and stop locations will not necessarily change current route nor dwell times if well designed and coordinated with MBTA; the city needs to assist in evolving this transit hub into a more dignified Square/Plaza for residents, visitors, and those transferring
