properties.request_other: Daily near-miss pedestrian hazard at Border St & Central Sq. Drivers often roll stop sign and enter crosswalk while people are crossing. Frequent unsafe conditions needing Vision Zero review.
properties.comments:
I am submitting a serious pedestrian safety concern for Border Street and Central Square in East Boston.

I cross this intersection multiple times per day and regularly experience near-miss incidents where vehicles fail to fully stop at the stop sign and enter or encroach into the marked crosswalk while pedestrians are actively crossing. This is a consistent daily pattern of unsafe driver behavior and failure to yield.

This creates a high-risk pedestrian environment at a residential crossing with frequent foot traffic.

There has also been a confirmed fatal pedestrian crash at the nearby intersection of Meridian Street and Central Square within the past year, indicating elevated risk in this corridor.

Given repeated near-misses, stop-sign noncompliance, and proximity to a recent fatality, I request urgent Vision Zero review as a connected safety corridor, including enforcement and engineering interventions such as daylighting, curb extensions, or raised crosswalks.
I'm a longtime resident at this corner, and I have concerns about the constant speeding on Richmond Street. People do not stop at the stop signs between dusk and dawn. Late night racing is a problem.

Drivers routinely run the stop signs at the intersection of Richmond and Butler Streets. Drivers speed down these streets every day, all day. Drivers have hit telephone poles, trees, and parked cars along these streets. Our own car was smashed into by an out of control driver a couple of years ago when it was parked on Richmond. Walking in the crosswalk feels dangerous since drivers don't even slow down at the stop signs. At one point these streets were on the list for speed bump installation but then we were removed from the list. No idea why since it would help the situation here. There is a school at the corner of Richmond and Dorchester, there are children and elderly in the neighborhood. People just want to feel safe walking and living here.

I was nearly hit by a cyclist speeding down the sidewalk, going at least 20 mph. She then proceeded to flip me off for not getting out of her way and then nearly plowed through a crowd of pedestrians behind me, as well as another cyclist. She also looked like she was wearing scrubs so I assume she works at one of the hospitals nearby. I'm sorry - how is this behavior ok?

I live on Horace and countless people are bypassing Bennington St by taking Horace St (between Harmony St and Moore St).  They are driving well above the speed limit and there are children on this road.  We need some drive slow signage.  Would be nice to have someone monitor the speed people are driving on this road.

The entire bike lane along Cambridge St. near MGH is essentially serving as a pick-up and drop-off area for drivers (including Ubers, taxis, also private vehicles) who collect or drop off patients at MGH or are just getting their takeout. Every. Single. Time that I walk or bike down this street, the lanes are completely blocked with multiple drivers stopped. I often ask them to move/remind them that it's a bike lane and just get the same response: that it's none of my business. I've reported this to Boston 311 many times and have still never seen anyone ticketed. This bike lane is a joke.
Delivery drivers often shoot through this intersection at red lights or weave in and out of bike lanes on this street. I feel very unsafe walking here.
The bike lane is so potholed that you need a mountain bike to navigate it. Or else bike in the middle of the road in front of cars.

at the corner of Amory Street and School Street in Jamaica Plain, the crosswalk is not very visible to people coming up the hill from the south. it's a very dangerous pedestrian crossing with a lot of school-age kids. we really need a push button flasher to warn people in cars that someone is crossing the street. It's only a matter of time before there is a pedestrian fatality. at the very least it needs daylighting

The whole stretch of Washington Street around the Egleston Square area (particularly from Columbus Ave to Forest Hills St) is very dangerous for bikes - there's no bike lane, the street is narrow and there is heavy traffic at nearly all hours. 

After getting doored on this stretch a few years back (despite riding at 10mph, using lights and being aware of my surroundings) and getting a concussion, I've avoided riding on this street despite the convenience it would offer. I hope that someday it will be safe to ride once again.

Drivers and motorcycles/mopeds speed constantly on MLK Jr Blvd, throughout the day but also at night - I live near the street so I hear them racing past again and again throughout the night. I wish there were some speed bumps or other traffic calming measures to slow people down in the stretches between the traffic lights.

Most of Magazine Street, but especially the part between Cedric Street and Mass Ave, has so many potholes (and old sewer drains that rise up instead of laying flat) that it's difficult and unsafe to bike - bikers are forced to veer into the center of the lane because the potholes take up the usual biking space. There are so many potholes I don't even know where to start with a 311 pothole request- the whole stretch of street just needs to be repaved. For anyone working or visiting 1010, improving this stretch would mean a safer way to commute.

Columbus Ave after Ruggles needs substantial improvement. The roadway needs to be paved and maintenanced. The bike lanes are not usable due to the conditions and bikes are at risk of being doored. This requires cyclists to ride in the middle of the lane in front of cars which is not safe.
Being at the end of the SW corridor, Dartmouth St NEEDS appropriate bike travel lanes in both directions to either Stuart St or Columbus.
People speed much faster than posted limits in a very residential and pedestrian heavy roadway. There should be a limit of 25 mph and speed humps.

I work at 1010 so I go through this intersection about twice a day. When the light switches to red and the pedestrian crossing light turns on, at least one and sometimes two cars run the red light, especially at the morning and evening rush hours. Pedestrians are constantly at risk crossing here. I wish someday there could be cameras that would catch license plates every time someone runs the light.

Bikes need protection approaching the curb cut to the sidewalk for the Arborway. Vehicles will drive over the buffer and the bike lane in advance of the roadway widening from one lane to two. I was nearly hit when a vehicle sped past me just as I was approaching the curb cut. Putting some sort of barrier (flexpost or a raised curb) in the buffer would prevent vehicles from entering the second lane too soon and endangering bicyclists.

I avoid the rotary by traveling between the Arborway carriage road and Orchard St. Admittedly, I bike the wrong way on Orchard St, but this is safer than biking on the Arborway north of Center St. But having a crosswalk and RRFB across Center St at Orchard St would make things safer for me. It would also put a crosswalk where there are bus stops. The nearest crosswalk is ~500' at Ballard St.

The Emerald Necklace pathway is halfway covered by overgrown bushes. It reduces the path to a single lane, which is unsafe because it is around a corner (so sight lines are limited) and on a hill, so bicyclists going downhill are going fast and may not see a bicyclist coming up the hill.
Drivers turning right are not respecting the crosswalk signals. Crossing needs to be divided up to allow for shorter walking segments for pedestrians who aren’t as fast.

I live on Alcott Street and it is always very difficult to see if cars/bikes are coming down Franklin street in either direction because cars are parked too close to the intersection. This seems like a perfect spot for some curb extensions to improve visibility and safety
This turn is dangerous and people speed up and down during rush hour
